correctness.rationale: For all aspect ratios a>=1 and 0<=theta<=pi/2, half-plane clipping lengths on two sides yield the explicit two-regime formula, with endpoints checked separately. Differentiation gives the unique diagonal stationary minimum when present, the switching-angle local maximum, and exact equality of diagonal and perpendicular values only at a=sqrt(2). A standalone half-plane clipping checker passed 21,344 independently constructed numerical tests; finite tests supplement rather than replace proof.

value.rationale: A complete natural planar convex-overlap perimeter optimization problem is solved over all rotations and all aspect ratios, not a numerical exercise at fixed sample parameters. Two distinct exact thresholds appear: a first-order global optimizer switch at sqrt(2), and disappearance of a locally stable diagonal optimum at 1+sqrt(2). A polygon-intersection perimeter optimizer can serve as a rigorous benchmark; the theorem is scoped to its geometric family and does not claim general convex-body implications.
